title: A constant-rank locally free module over a semilocal ring has a basis
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative semilocal ring, meaning that $R$ has only finitely many maximal ideals, and let $M$ be an $R$-module. Let $n\geq0$ be an integer. Assume that there are finitely many elements $t_1,\ldots,t_m\in R$ generating the unit ideal such that $M_{t_i}$ is a free $R_{t_i}$-module with a basis of $n$ elements for every $i$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Then $M$ has an $R$-basis indexed by $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, equivalently $M\cong R^{\oplus n}$. The zero ring, $n=0$, and an empty principal cover of the zero ring are allowed.

source.place: Tag 02M9, lemma-locally-free-semi-local-free; constant rank expressed by a finite principal-open free cover.

proof.text: If $R$ is the zero ring, every $z\in M$ satisfies $z=1z=0z=0$. Thus $R^{\oplus n}\to M$ is the unique bijection, and the all-zero family indexed by $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ is a basis by [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. This covers the empty principal cover as well. Henceforth suppose $R\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 02M9, lemma-locally-free-semi-local-free, proof hints; explicit finite Chinese-remainder construction.

proof.text: Enumerate the finitely many distinct maximal ideals as $\mathfrak q_1,\ldots,\mathfrak q_s$. For every $a$, some $t_i$ lies outside $\mathfrak q_a$: otherwise their unit-ideal linear combination $1$ would belong to $\mathfrak q_a$. Apply [lem-a1-local-trivialization-residue-rank] to this $t_i$, with $E=R$, $P=M$ and $r=n$. It gives $M_{\mathfrak q_a}\cong R_{\mathfrak q_a}^{\oplus n}$ and $\dim_{R/\mathfrak q_a}(M/\mathfrak q_aM)=n$. Choose a basis $(\bar x_{a,k})_{1\le k\le n}$ of each of these residue modules and representatives $x_{a,k}\in M$.

source.place: Tag 02M9, lemma-locally-free-semi-local-free, proof hints; explicit finite Chinese-remainder construction.

proof.text:
For $a
e b$, the ideal $\mathfrak q_a+\mathfrak q_b$ strictly contains $\mathfrak q_a$ (distinct maximal ideals cannot contain one another), hence equals $R$. Choose $u_{ab}\in\mathfrak q_b$ and $v_{ab}\in\mathfrak q_a$ with $u_{ab}+v_{ab}=1$. Put $e_a=\prod_{b
e a}u_{ab}$. Modulo $\mathfrak q_a$ every factor is $1$, so $e_a\equiv1$; modulo $\mathfrak q_b$ for $b
e a$ the factor $u_{ab}$ is zero, so $e_a\equiv0$. The empty product when $s=1$ is $1$. This proves the needed Chinese-remainder weights directly from maximality, without asserting that the $e_a$ are idempotent.

source.place: Tag 02M9, lemma-locally-free-semi-local-free, proof hints; explicit finite Chinese-remainder construction.

proof.text: For $1\le k\le n$ define $x_k=\sum_{a=1}^s e_ax_{a,k}$. In $M/\mathfrak q_bM$ this sum reduces to $\bar x_{b,k}$ by the congruences of step 3. Thus the images of the single family $(x_k)$ form a basis in every maximal residue module. For $n=0$ all these families are empty; the same calculation is vacuous and valid.

source.place: Tag 02M9, lemma-locally-free-semi-local-free, proof hints; explicit finite Chinese-remainder construction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-basis-of-maximal-residue-bases] with $E=R$, $P=M$, $r=n$ and the prescribed vectors $x_k$. Its maximal-localization hypothesis is exactly step 2, and its prescribed-residue-basis hypothesis is step 4. It yields that $R^{\oplus n}\to M$, $(c_k)\mapsto\sum_k c_kx_k$, is bijective, equivalently that $(x_k)_{1\le k\le n}$ is the required $R$-basis. Its statement includes rank zero.
